# Remote job scouting

Read the owner's preferences from memory first: target lanes, state/country and work authorization, computer/OS, physical limits, and pay floor. Scouting only; never apply.

## 1. Find roles
- Pull postings from public ATS job-board APIs rather than scraping job boards:
  - Greenhouse: `https://boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<board>/jobs?content=true`
  - Lever: `https://api.lever.co/v0/postings/<company>?mode=json`
  - Ashby: `https://api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/<org>?includeCompensation=true`
- Favor remote-first companies that hire beginners: SaaS support and customer success, AI evaluation and training roles, junior dev/QA, tech support, operations, sales.

## 2. Filter
- Keep only fully remote roles that allow the owner's state/country and work authorization.
- Skip roles requiring a degree ("or equivalent experience" is fine), student status, or physical work the owner can't do.
- Keep only laptop-friendly roles that work on the owner's computer/OS (drop e.g. Windows-only tooling for a Mac user).
- Prefer full-time or steady part-time over gig/piecework tasking platforms.

## 3. Scam check (drop any that fail)
- The posting lives on the company's own careers page or a real ATS board for that company, and the company has a real site and footprint.
- No upfront fees, equipment purchases, check deposits, gift cards, crypto, or "reshipping".
- No interviews by chat app only, no requests for SSN or bank details before an offer, no pay that's far above market for the work.
- Recruiter emails come from the company's own domain.

## 4. Verify and record
- Fetch each actual posting to confirm it's open. Record company, title, location text, pay if listed, degree language, posting URL, and a one-line fit note.
- Read the tracker CSV first and right before writing; skip any role already there (same company+title or URL). Append rows only, keep the existing columns (default: `id,company,title,location,platform,url,fit,notes,status`, status `queued`), and give each row a unique id.

## 5. Hand off
- Message the owner's applying bot with the new ids and the top picks to apply to first.
- Send the owner a short summary: how many added, the top 5 with links, and how many were rejected and why.

---
name: remote-scout-getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner of a remote-job scouting bot,
  to learn what to look for.
---
I find verified, open remote jobs that don't need a degree and work from your laptop, filter out scams, add them to a job tracker spreadsheet, and hand them to your applying bot.

Ask these one at a time, conversationally, and adapt to the answers:
1. Your background: ask them to attach their resume (or describe their experience), and save it on the computer.
2. Location and work authorization: which state/country they live in, whether they're authorized to work there, and whether they need sponsorship.
3. Target lanes: which kinds of roles (e.g. support, AI evaluation, junior dev/QA, ops, sales), pay floor, hours, and any physical limits.
4. Computer: what computer and operating system they'll work on (Mac, Windows, Chromebook), so roles fit their setup.
5. Handoff: where the tracker CSV should live, and which applying bot (if any) should get new finds.

Save each answer to memory, create the tracker CSV if there isn't one, then start the remote-job-scouting skill and offer a weekly routine for fresh scouting passes.
